_comment: WO-1223 - THE DUNGEON COVERAGE MANIFEST. The one artifact both halves of the
portal gate can read.
WHY IT EXISTS: the list of dungeons a player can REACH is client-side (a table
in DungeonWorldPortalSpawner plus the build scene list). The list of doors that
can be CLOSED is server-side (the dungeon_status rows in Neon). Neither side
could see the other, so a reachable dungeon with no row was invisible to every
gate in the repo - which is exactly how dg_healers_cottage shipped reachable,
populated and ungateable, and black-screened the owner with nothing to flip.
SO THIS FILE IS THE CONTRACT, and BOTH sides assert against it:
* Unity  - Assets/Editor/Regression/DungeonStatusRegression.cs case
[door-coverage] asserts this list is EXACTLY the set of dungeon ids
the player can reach, computed from the AuthoredPortals table INTERSECT
the LoadDefs injections INTERSECT the enabled EditorBuildSettings scenes.
It cannot be hand-edited into agreement: add an entry that is not
reachable, or ship a dungeon that is not listed here, and it reds.
* Node   - test/dungeon-status.manifest.test.js asserts every 'portal-gated'
entry has a dungeon_status row in api/schema.sql, and that schema.sql
seeds no id this manifest does not carry.
IT IS DELIBERATELY A DUPLICATE of state that lives in C#, and CLAUDE.md is right
that duplicated state is how canon rots. The duplication is unavoidable - node
cannot read a C# array - so it is GUARDED instead: the Unity case asserts the two
against each other in both directions, so this file cannot drift without reddening.
accounting values (the Unity case pins each one against a C# list):
portal-gated  - id is in DungeonStatusCatalog.PortalDungeonIds. It has a door,
the door can be closed from the server, and it MUST have a row.
not-gated     - id is in DungeonStatusRegression.MustNotBeGated. Reachable, but
deliberately outside this system, and 'reason' says why.
unaccounted   - reachable and in NEITHER list. This is a FINDING for the owner,
never something an implementer quietly resolves by picking a list.
The Unity case FAILS on every one of these, by name, on purpose.
OWNER RULING 2026-08-26 (WO-1223), verbatim: 'not acesable if not in table, if in
table and works then yes'. Two consequences, both live in the tree now:
1. dg_folks_granary and dg_healers_cottage moved unaccounted -> portal-gated.
2. THE CLIENT DEFAULT INVERTED. DungeonStatusCatalog.For no longer resolves an
absent id / absent table / rejected payload / unparseable status to OPEN - all
of those are now CLOSED. So a 'portal-gated' entry with no dungeon_status row
is no longer merely ungateable: it is SHUT to every player. Seeding the row is
mandatory, and test/dungeon-status.manifest.test.js is what makes it mandatory.
THE COPY RULE TRAVELS WITH THE DATA (api/dungeon-status.js header): a closed
dungeon reads as WORLD. Nothing in this file is player-facing, but the headline
and body that seal one of these ids must be authored prose, never build status.

dungeons.reason: East portal. Composed starter loop; the first crawl the player meets.

The Rootways is a CROSSROADS, not a dungeon: one mouth, four arms into the biomes. Its portal row is DERIVED (DungeonWorldPortalSpawner.TryDeriveHollowRoadsPortal), not authored, and it is switched by FeatureFlags.BiomeRoads rather than by a door state. Gating it here would gate something that has no dungeon behind it.

West portal, restored 2026-08-22 pointing at the composed graph. RULED GATABLE by the owner 2026-08-26 (WO-1223: 'not acesable if not in table, if in table and works then yes'), so it joined PortalDungeonIds and now fails CLOSED until dungeon_status carries a row for it.

South portal, re-pointed 2026-08-22 to the composed graph, and the one that cost the owner the black screen - she was standing in it ([Flow:HeroOwner] scene='dg_healers_cottage', 7 enemies) with no row to flip. RULED GATABLE by the owner 2026-08-26 (WO-1223), so it joined PortalDungeonIds and now fails CLOSED until dungeon_status carries a row for it.
